details.excerpt:
Retail evaluation rules (real-v1)

The attached CSV is a row-preserving slice of the UCI Online Retail workbook containing every source row whose InvoiceDate falls in January 2011. InvoiceNo is an invoice identifier; rows are invoice lines and should not be treated as unique invoices.

For qualifying sales questions, include a row only when InvoiceNo does not begin with C (case-insensitive), Quantity is greater than zero, and UnitPrice is greater than zero. Sales are Quantity multiplied by UnitPrice and are denominated in GBP. Preserve missing CustomerID as missing; do not infer identities. Dates in this slice use the workbook's local timestamps. These rules define an evaluation convention and do not claim to be UCI's official accounting policy.

segments.text: What factors does the opening summary of the inflation chapter associate with price pressures in FY22 and FY23? Cite the passage and distinguish external supply/commodity factors from food-price conditions.

trials.answer_text:
The opening summary links two sets of drivers to the price pressures seen in FY 22‑23:

1. **External supply‑side and commodity pressures** – It cites “supply disruptions inflicted by the pandemic” and “increased commodity prices caused by heightened global conflicts” as the forces that pushed up core consumer‑goods and services prices.
2. **Food‑price conditions** – It notes that “food prices were affected by adverse weather conditions in the last two years,” indicating that weather‑driven agricultural supply issues drove food‑price pressure.

Thus, the chapter attributes FY 22‑23 price pressures to (a) pandemic‑related supply chain shocks and rising global commodity prices, and (b) weather‑related food‑price pressures.

details.excerpt:
CHAPTER

03PRICES AND INFLATION:

UNDER CONTROL

The pandemic and subsequent geo-political tensions presented considerable challenges

to the global economy in inflation management. The supply disruptions inflicted by

the pandemic and increased commodity prices caused by heightened global conflicts

markedly affected India. As a result, FY22 and FY23 witnessed price pressures in core

consumer goods and services. Food prices were affected by adverse weather conditions

in the last two years. The net impact of these developments was elevated inflationary

pressures in FY23 and FY24. Prudent monetary policy response and calibrated trade

policy measures by the Government, coupled with strong output growth, helped reduce

core inflation to a four-year low in FY24. Appropriate administrative actions, including

dynamic stock management, open market operations, subsidised provision of essential

food items and trade policy measures, helped mitigate food inflation to a great extent.

The expectation of a normal monsoon and moderating global prices of key imported

items give credence to the benign and range-bound inflation projections for India made

by the Reserve Bank of India and the International Monetary Fund. Beyond this, the

medium to long-term inflation outlook will be shaped by the strengthening of price

monitoring mechanisms and market intelligence as well as focussed efforts to increase

the domestic production of essential food items like pulses and edible oils for which

India has a great degree of import dependence.

the domestic production of essential food items like pulses and edible oils for which

segments.text: इस हिंदी अध्याय के अनुसार FY24 में खुदरा मुद्रास्फीति और खाद्य मुद्रास्फीति के बारे में क्या कहा गया है? मुद्रास्फीति अध्याय में मूल साक्ष्य दें।

trials.answer_text:
वित्तीय वर्ष 24 (FY24) में भारत की खुदरा मुद्रास्फीति में स्पष्ट गिरावट आई।

- अखिल भारतीय औसत खुदरा मुद्रास्फीति दर FY24 में घटकर लगभग **5.4 %** तक रही, जो कोविड‑19 महामारी के बाद का सबसे निचला स्तर है [evidence:df5dee0a-6303-4a72-8c36-b008e3f1322a].
- जून 2024 में खुदरा मुद्रास्फीति **5.1 %** तक पहुँच गई [evidence:70041154-8f3e-4e5d-8ee2-9c7d41ae1cd3].
- राज्य‑स्तर पर, 36 में से 29 राज्यों और केंद्र शासित प्रदेशों की मुद्रास्फीति दर **6 %** से नीचे रही [evidence:43f1883b-75cd-45c8-bd4f-55adb1f2c119].

खाद्य‑विषयक मुद्रास्फीति के बारे में कहा गया है कि:

- वित्त वर्ष 24 में खाद्य मुद्रास्फीति को नियंत्रित करने के लिए सरकार ने गेहूँ/आटा, चावल, प्याज आदि के निर्यात पर प्रतिबंध, स्टॉक सीमा, और किफायती आटा की सब्सिडी जैसी प्रशासनिक उपाय लागू किए [evidence:686b3439-70dd-44d7-8c08-d2432025f706].
- ऊर्जा और कोर मुद्रास्फीति में गिरावट के कारण, FY24 में खाद्य कीमतों में अस्थिरता के बावजूद **हेडलाइन मुद्रास्फीति में गिरावट** सुनिश्चित हुई [evidence:776f2251-84ed-4858-b149-e4996a31e38f].

संक्षेप में, FY24 में खुदरा मुद्रास्फीति लगभग 5 % के आसपास स्थिर रही, जबकि खाद्य मुद्रास्फीति को कम करने के लिये विशेष नीति‑उपाय अपनाए गये और कुल मिलाकर हेडलाइन मुद्रास्फीती में गिरावट आई।

- वित्त वर्ष 24 में खाद्य मुद्रास्फीति को नियंत्रित करने के लिए सरकार ने गेहूँ/आटा, चावल, प्याज आदि के निर्यात पर प्रतिबंध, स्टॉक सीमा, और किफायती आटा की सब्सिडी जैसी प्रशासनिक उपाय लागू किए [evidence:686b3439-70dd-44d7-8c08-d2432025f706].
- ऊर्जा और कोर मुद्रास्फीति में गिरावट के कारण, FY24 में खाद्य कीमतों में अस्थिरता के बावजूद **हेडलाइन मुद्रास्फीति में गिरावट** सुनिश्चित हुई [evidence:776f2251-84ed-4858-b149-e4996a31e38f].

details.reason: Verify both documents are cited for the same FY24 measure and period.

observations.answer_text: Both the full Economic Survey PDF and the standalone inflation chapter contain a dedicated chapter on Prices and Inflation (see e16 from the full PDF and e17 from the standalone PDF). In the full Economic Survey, the chapter reports that retail inflation declined to **5.4 % in FY24** (e15). The standalone inflation chapter states that India “successfully managed to keep retail inflation at **5.4 % in FY24**” (e28). Thus, the FY24 retail‑inflation figure is the same in both documents, indicating agreement between the two sources.

inflationary pressures moderated in FY24. After averaging 6.7 per cent in FY23, retail inflation

declined to 5.4 per cent in FY24. This has been due to the combination of measures undertaken

by the Government and the RBI. The Union Government undertook prompt measures such as

open market sales, retailing in specified outlets, timely imports, reduced the prices of Liquified

Petroleum Gas (LPG) cylinders and implemented a cut in petrol and diesel prices. The RBI

raised policy rates by a cumulative 250 bps between May 2022 and February 2023. It also

managed liquidity levels efficiently and maintained consistent and coherent communication

with market participants. Even as higher policy rates are transmitted through the system, the

RBI continues to support growth with adequate liquidity, thereby ensuring that inflation is

headed to the target of 4 per cent on a durable basis. The effects of these measures are reflected

in the latest data on CPI inflation – headline CPI inflation of 5.1 per cent in June 2024, and core

inflation declined to 3.1 per cent. Consequently, India was the only country amongst its peers

to traverse a high-growth and low-inflation path in the period FY

CHAPTER

03PRICES AND INFLATION:

UNDER CONTROL

The pandemic and subsequent geo-political tensions presented considerable challenges

to the global economy in inflation management. The supply disruptions inflicted by

the pandemic and increased commodity prices caused by heightened global conflicts

markedly affected India. As a result, FY22 and FY23 witnessed price pressures in core

consumer goods and services. Food prices were affected by adverse weather conditions

in the last two years. The net impact of these developments was elevated inflationary

pressures in FY23 and FY24. Prudent monetary policy response and calibrated trade

policy measures by the Government, coupled with strong output growth, helped reduce

core inflation to a four-year low in FY24. Appropriate administrative actions, including

dynamic stock management, open market operations, subsidised provision of essential

food items and trade policy measures, helped mitigate food inflation to a great extent.

The expectation of a normal monsoon and moderating global prices of key imported

items give credence to the benign and range-bound inflation projections for India made

The pandemic and subsequent geo-political tensions presented considerable challenges

to the global economy in inflation management. The supply disruptions inflicted by

the pandemic and increased commodity prices caused by heightened global conflicts

core inflation to a four-year low in FY24. Appropriate administrative actions, including

dynamic stock management, open market operations, subsidised provision of essential

food items and trade policy measures, helped mitigate food inflation to a great extent.

dynamic stock management, open market operations, subsidised provision of essential

आर्थिक सर्वेक्षण, वर्ष 2023-24 चार्ट प्ा.11: कोर का इसके घटकों में विभाजन — fears मुद्रास्फीति — 'टिकाऊ मुद्रास्फीति 3.12. महामारी के बाद से, उच्च स्तर के खाद्य मुद्रास्फीति में कमी के कारण भारत में मुद्रास्फीतिक दबाव वित्त वर्ष 22 में कम हो गया। तथापि, कोर मुद्रास्फीति उसी समय 6 प्रतिशत तक बढ़ गई थी, जो मुख्य रूप से अंतर्राष्ट्रीय वस्तुओं की बढ़ती कीमतों से प्रभावित थी। जैसा कि चार्ट ae में दर्शाया गया है, वर्ष में कोर सेवाओं की मुद्रास्फीति बढ़ी, लेकिन यह बढ़त कोर उपभोक्ता वस्तुओं की तुलना में कम थी। 3.13. वित्त वर्ष 23 में मुद्रास्फीतिक संबंधी दबाव फिर से रूस-यूक्रेन युद्ध से प्रभावित होकर बढ़ गया, जिससे आपूर्ति gaat बाधित हुई और खाद्य व ईंधन की कीमतों में वृद्धि हुई। जैसे-जैसे आर्थिक गतिविधि में तेजी आयी, कोर मुद्रास्फीति में भी थोड़ी वृद्धि हुई और यह मुख्य रूप से कोर सेवाओं की मुद्रास्फीति से प्रभावित हुई क्योंकि लोगों के शहरी क्षेत्रों में लौटने के साथ घर के किराए में वृद्धि हुई (चार्ट M115)! वित्त वर्ष 24 में, कीमतों में सुधार हुआ। कोर मुद्रास्फीति - वस्तु और सेवा दोनों में कमी के कारण सीपीआई मुद्रास्फीति में कमी आयी। वित्त वर्ष 24 में कोर सेवा मुद्रास्फीति नौ साल के निचले स्तर पर आ गई; वहीं, कोर वस्तु मुद्रास्फीति भी घटकर चार साल के निचले स्तर पर आ गई। 3.

segments.text: In the statistical appendix, locate Table 4.3, All India Consumer Price Index Numbers. Identify the table's coverage categories and report the source page numbers; do not calculate a trend unless the correct column and period are clear.

trials.answer_text: Table 4.3 in the Statistical Appendix (Economic Survey 2023‑24) covers three CPI series: Industrial Workers (CPI‑IW), the New Series for Agricultural Labourers (CPI‑NS) and Rural Labourers (CPI‑RL). For the CPI‑IW series the table provides four sub‑categories – General, Rural, Urban and Combined – while the CPI‑NS and CPI‑RL series are shown as General indices. The table appears on page 92 (the main historical data) and continues on page 93 with the latest 2024‑25 provisional figures.

segments.text: Does the chapter establish that adverse weather alone caused India's FY24 food inflation? Use the cited evidence to distinguish reported contributing conditions from a claim of a single proven cause.

trials.answer_text: The chapter does **not** establish that adverse weather alone caused India’s FY24 food inflation. It repeatedly describes adverse weather as one of several factors influencing food prices, alongside other conditions such as supply disruptions from the pandemic, geopolitical tensions, and domestic policy measures. For example, the text notes that “Food prices were affected by adverse weather conditions in the last two years” (e1) and lists a range of weather‑related events (heat waves, uneven monsoon, hailstorms, etc.) that contributed to higher food inflation (e2). Additionally, it mentions that “excessive heat in the summer and uneven rainfall put pressure on food prices” while also referencing external shocks like the Russia‑Ukraine war (e7). None of these passages claim that adverse weather was the sole or singular cause; they present it as a contributing condition among multiple influences.

03PRICES AND INFLATION:

UNDER CONTROL

The pandemic and subsequent geo-political tensions presented considerable challenges

to the global economy in inflation management. The supply disruptions inflicted by

the pandemic and increased commodity prices caused by heightened global conflicts

markedly affected India. As a result, FY22 and FY23 witnessed price pressures in core

consumer goods and services. Food prices were affected by adverse weather conditions

in the last two years. The net impact of these developments was elevated inflationary
